newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil cargo premiums firm, barge premiums ease.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil cargo premiums firm, barge premiums ease.

text.p: NWE gas oil was perkier on Tuesday with cargo premiums edging up on prospects of tighter supplies. Barge premiums, however lost ground on poor prompt buying.
April IPE gas oil closed $1.25 a tonne stronger at $172.00.

Heating oil barges bucked the generally bullish trend with premiums actually falling. Traders said demand was lacklustre from German buyers, with two 2,000 tonne barges going at April IPE -$1.25 fob ARA, a drop of about 50 cents.

Russian premiums were steady, unable to rise higher because of the lack of material. Premiums for 2H Russian were around April +$2-3 cif NWE, but nearly all material has been committed for arbitraging to Asia.
A small 6,000 tonne parcel was done at mean of means +$9 cif Germany.

FOD premiums were being pushed by buying interest being met by almost no material. A cargo that was offered at April IPE +$4.50 cif NWE, up $1 or so, was later withdrawn. Traders thought the material might head to Spain.

DIN material eased off very slightly in the afternoon following a morning trade at April IPE +$7 cif Germany March 20-30 and was heard offered pegged around April IPE +$6.75. April 1-10 dates was understood to be pegged around April IPE +$5 cif.

The diesel market gained some support from news that Poland will increase imports of gasoline and diesel fuel to 2.5 million tonnes in 1997 from 900,000 tonnes in 1996. Traders said they did not expect any significant price gains since the increase would be spread out over the year.
An EN590 25-30kt cargo traded at April IPE +$12 cif NWE for second half, a price that reflected the market for summer spec material.
